hypothesis: BRCA1 silencing in TNBC operates through a dual-layered mechanism — germline/somatic mutation AND epigenetic promoter methylation (constitutional + tumoral) — that produces functionally equivalent HRD phenotypes, yet current PARPi eligibility criteria screen only for mutation status; this gap means ~20% of constitutionally BRCA1-methylated TNBC patients (who exhibit full HRD genomic scarring) are systematically excluded from PARPi trials, and pharmacological induction of BRCAness via RAD51 destabilization (e.g., ivabradine-mediated FBXO24 upregulation) can functionally reconstitute PARPi sensitivity in the non-gBRCAm majority, suggesting that HRD functional state — not genotype — should be the treatment-selection axis.

evidence.source: PMID:41654537 — Pasanisi J et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2026 Feb 7
evidence.claim: Constitutional BRCA1 methylation detected in 20.6% of 136 TNBC patients; tumoral methylation in 31.6%; cases with constitutional methylation show high tumoral methylation co-occurrence and genomic instability consistent with HRD (LOH, TAI, LST scars)

evidence.source: PMID:40764992 — Tsoi H et al., J Transl Med 2025 Aug 5
evidence.claim: Ivabradine promotes RAD51 proteasomal degradation via ATF6-driven FBXO24 upregulation, inducing BRCAness in non-gBRCAm TNBC cells and synergistically potentiating olaparib efficacy in vitro; DR-GFP and EJ5-GFP assays confirm HR pathway suppression

evidence.source: PMID:40864792 — Shah B et al., Curr Issues Mol Biol 2025 Aug 8
evidence.claim: HRD prevalence in TNBC is 50–70%; detection integrates genomic scars (LOH/TAI/LST), COSMIC SBS3 signature, and functional RAD51 foci assays achieving >90% sensitivity; BRCA reversion mutations and SETD1A/EME1/SOX5 pathways drive PARPi resistance

evidence.source: PMID:40819058 — Peng X et al., Mol Cancer 2025 Aug 16
evidence.claim: Jab1 (CSN5) stabilizes HRR-gene mRNAs (including BRCA1, RAD51) via mRNA stability regulation; Jab1 overexpression in TNBC confers PARPi resistance; Jab1 inhibition resensitizes TNBC to olaparib in vivo

evidence.source: PMID:41900138 — Huang L et al., Molecules 2026 Mar 20
evidence.claim: Epacadostat (IDO1 inhibitor) combined with olaparib suppresses BRCA1 and RAD51 expression in BRCA-proficient TNBC, achieving synergistic growth inhibition — demonstrating that immune-metabolic pathway interference can downregulate HR competency

evidence.source: PMID:41854792 — Masuda N et al., Breast Cancer Res Treat 2026 Mar 19
evidence.claim: In the randomized JBCRG-22 trial, HRD-positive TNBC patients showed significantly better long-term outcomes with eribulin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy, validating HRD status as a predictive (not merely prognostic) biomarker for non-PARPi regimens

Tumoral BRCA1 promoter hypermethylation (somatic epigenetic, ~31.6% TNBC)

Jab1/CSN5 mRNA stability axis: controls steady-state levels of BRCA1, RAD51, PALB2 transcripts
IDO1 pathway crosstalk: epacadostat-induced metabolic shift suppresses HR gene expression

Functional assays: RAD51 foci by immunofluorescence (gold standard for HR activity)
Epigenetic: BRCA1 promoter methylation profiling (blood + tumor paired)

emerging_targets.novelty: High — mechanism identified 2025, not yet in clinical trials

emerging_targets.novelty: High — 2025 discovery linking mRNA stability to PARPi resistance

emerging_targets.novelty: Medium — IDO1 inhibitors known; HR downregulation mechanism is novel 2026 finding

clinical_relevance.current_eligibility_gap: PARPi approvals (olaparib, talazoparib) require germline BRCA1/2 mutation; TNBC patients with equivalent HRD via epigenetic silencing or BRCAness-induction are excluded from standard of care
clinical_relevance.biomarker_implication: RAD51 foci functional assay combined with BRCA1 methylation profiling could expand PARPi-eligible TNBC population by an estimated 25–35% beyond current germline-mutation criteria
clinical_relevance.trial_context: JBCRG-22 randomized data (2026) establishes HRD status as predictive for eribulin response, not just PARPi — HRD testing should inform all chemotherapy selection in TNBC, not only PARP inhibitor candidacy
clinical_relevance.combination_strategies: ADC-PARPi combinations (2025 review, PMID:40494034) and ATR+PARPi (PMID:41595228) are active investigation areas to address BRCA-reversion resistance

research_gaps: No prospective trial testing PARPi eligibility based on constitutional BRCA1 methylation rather than germline mutation status
Jab1 inhibitors lack clinical-stage compounds; target validation is preclinical only
Ivabradine-olaparib combination untested in vivo tumor models beyond cell lines; no pharmacokinetic data in TNBC context
RAD51 foci assay not yet standardized across clinical labs — threshold for 'HR-deficient' designation varies (typically <10% RAD51+ cells post-irradiation)
Relationship between constitutional BRCA1 methylation, tumoral methylation, and immune microenvironment (PD-L1, TIL density) unexplored in TNBC
Whether IDO1-mediated HR suppression is reversible or creates durable BRCAness is unknown
novelty_claim: The synthesis reveals a convergent BRCAness induction framework: regardless of mechanism (germline mutation, epigenetic silencing via constitutional/tumoral methylation, or pharmacological RAD51 destabilization via FBXO24/Jab1 axes), the therapeutic-relevant state is functional HR incompetence detectable by RAD51 foci assay — not genotype. The novel connection is that Jab1 (mRNA stability) and FBXO24 (protein stability) represent parallel post-transcriptional control points for HR capacity that could be co-targeted with PARPi in the ~50% of BRCA-wildtype TNBC currently ineligible for PARPi, and that BRCA1 constitutional methylation creates an inherited epigenetic BRCAness phenotype that warrants reclassification as a hereditary BRCA1-equivalent risk category.
actionability: Design a 2x2 in vitro experiment in TNBC cell lines (MDA-MB-231 as BRCA1-wt; HCC1937 as BRCA1-mutant controls): (1) Jab1 siRNA knockdown + olaparib vs. (2) ivabradine (FBXO24 inducer) + olaparib, measuring RAD51 foci formation by immunofluorescence, HR efficiency by DR-GFP reporter assay, and cell viability by CellTiter-Glo — to determine whether Jab1 suppression and FBXO24 activation are additive, synergistic, or redundant routes to BRCAness induction in BRCA1-proficient TNBC.
